text:
I’m a passionate and hard-working machine learning developer with 6 years of experience building practical Python-based solutions, and I’d be glad to help update your TensorFlow project from v1.15 to the latest version.

My background includes extensive experience with Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, and machine learning workflows. While my recent work has centered more on applied ML and NLP, I’m comfortable working through existing codebases, understanding how models and pipelines are structured, and making careful updates while preserving behavior.

One relevant project was Product recommendations for Tidewater Outfitters, where I built similar-items and you-may-also-like carousels trained on 1.2M interactions and cached in Redis. That work led to a 14% increase in click-through rate during a 4-week A/B test. Another project was Coffee review themes for Cobalt Coffee Roasters, where I built a small Streamlit app that grouped 38k marketplace reviews into themes and tracked sentiment per theme each week. That project produced 12 stable themes and replaced about 2 days a month of manual tagging.

For your TensorFlow update, I’d approach the migration carefully: review the current v1.15 implementation, identify deprecated APIs and session-based patterns, update the code to match the latest version’s best practices, and validate the project after the upgrade. I’m comfortable working iteratively and keeping the existing functionality intact while modernizing the implementation.

If helpful during the interview, I can also walk you through similar code adaptation work and discuss how I’d test the upgrade to reduce the risk of regressions. What parts of the project are most important to preserve exactly during the TensorFlow v1.15 to latest-version update?
